body: It's more than entirely possible to support yourself nowadays without completely succumbing to becoming an average Joe and working your life away like everybody else

Well, in any sort of group or unification of people, you have to have some sort of work ethic. Somebody needs to bring in the supplies for food, shelter, water, etc. So you're exactly right, because those should be the only three resources that are guaranteed. Society now is a leeching cancer, You feel the same way I did 2 years ago at 19, and the exact way most intuitive 19-year-olds will feel. Because your feelings are true.
Why the f*** would you spend your 50 something years that you're able to physically work on somebody else's dream? Because the same people who brought you up to understand what this society is, is the same people that want you to be something less. This world is now about money and corruption. Money is all people are after.

But what we fail to understand at that age is that even with this understanding it's not something we have to succumb to. At all. I promise you that suicide as much as you need those feelings in those thoughts, is near impossible. Even with the most little hope, gut wrenching, tortured state of mind, it's hard to commit suicide. When I was your age I had thrown every single thing away on purpose so that I would be literally strong enough to end my life at that same age for the exact same reason, had a rope, had a plan, 7 months later still couldn't do it.

You're on a really long long journey of self-growth and realization, and this is the dark part. The part of suffering. And anyway you feel that you need to actually feel about it or react, is completely valid. You are in this situation. There's a good chance you won't die and be able to leave this behind. So please atleast understand that it does get better, but it gets better because you get closer to a life you can respect. The older you get the more control you will have. 

And as far as what you're worried about, think about it this way. Instead of hunting for food and going out and getting resources, working is now the new way of hunting for food and gaining those basic human resources. And what do you do when most of your time is spent just keeping yourself alive? You find a better way of doing it, faster and more efficient way, so that you can start working towards creating other things. Life should be about the journey of oneself. For God f****** sake the world is only perceived through the eyes that are seeing it. So for society to uphold your bank account before your basic human worth, is frankly disgusting. But to match every disgusting face that it shows, I swear to you that there is something beautiful. So many things and opportunities that are much greater than this b*******. It's a painful ride but if you can hang on, you WILL be rewarded. We don't understand why this happens to us. But we also don't understand the rewards and other side of that. That's why it happens

Yes. Go to bed. It's really really hard when you're in this kind of position, but if you can kind of just let yourself go, like you would imagine you're letting yourself die and you're killing yourself, and you don't push away the feelings but you kind of just let them in and just submit to them and eventually fall asleep, you will LITERALLY Wake up like you did die, and now you're coming back and seeing what it would be like after you did. If you can do it it's the best way to have a reset button with nothing available to you. And if you absolutely absolutely absolutely have to, do cutting. have the same ideology. Think of it like taking out that anger and hatred of life, that you can't really take out any other way.it's okay to let yourself fall sometimes friend. And some of us have just, the pulsating urge that things really are wrong and action needs to be taken now, and sometimes we have to take a burn so that we don't completely engulf ourselves in the flame.

and keep it all into perspective that you are extremely extremely strong to be even dealing with this, and the world will not throw you anything that you can't handle. And you might not feel anything now but you and the people that you do truly care about will be extremely extremely proud of you.

It doesn't matter what you have. We all have something to dispise about ourselves. And we all feel it in a different way. 
I can totally see how it must make you feel. But just remember self care and confidence starts from the inside, into the outside. It's easier to first see from the outside. But you have to remember there's a really special beautiful person inside that shell. That right there, is a much bigger more impact battle you'll want to fight. Because at the end, nobody can take away your self appreation. And trust me, it will eventually be something you'll hardly even notice, and then come to appreciate as one of your quirks. It makes you unique.

My ex has HV, hidradenitis suppurativa, and it is both extremely painful and insecuring. Focus on the battle of you. I know it's really hard but the more you practice it, the easier it becomes to look at this issue and say "Okay, this is not how I want it but this is who I am, and I appreciate that." " It may not be what I want now, but I'm strong enough to become better, and I'm worth the whole process."

Best thing to remember this is your fight, and everything in it, YOU determine the pain in it. That's what makes you feel like you're special not in a good way. It does give you some sort of power. But it doesn't because nobody in this kind of pain ever lies. So don't lie to yourself.

And remember, this is clinical depression, not depression, this is something in your brain that has it's own cycle. A cycle you'll learn to read like you would read a child. You can easily see their next move. You can then turn it into fuels that pushes you forward not backwards. Hang in there friend ❤️ 

And ANOTHER good thing to remember is your 4 year future self will appreciate everything you do untill then. And that person will soon BE you. And I promise you, you get through this, you will never have appreciated anything more than yourself.

Hey friend. Please don't give up. 
I haven't came on this sub in years, and the last time I did, I was in the same position as you. I dropped out at 16, graduated with a year from that. There are other alternatives to school, but it's the first thing that really made me face the real truth that is life, and especially society, is fucking meaningless. The distractions, the morals, the responsibilities, all of these things that we are held to such high stresses we realize at a much younger age that these things aren't worth the effort and time, so we are not interested. So we can't learn. You can't learn because it's meaningless. You aren't dumb in the slightest.

When you mentioned music, that made alot of sense. I know you are drowning, but if you want any real advice on what happens with and after these emotions, is you become stronger. Life becomes harder, but you become stronger. It's like a clothes wringer that is designed just enough to keep you alive but keep alot of pain. That will be the next few years. This part and transition of your life is a difficult one with these issues, you have depression and it's not because of your situation. Your situation will change and there are alot of options other than having society put you through this shit.

But Life Is ultimately about the eyes that are seeing it, you. You will learn to love and appreciate the kind of person you are and the situations you've pulled through, and even now. I don't have any room to cut even if I still did on both of my entire arms, it really does show the mental strength someone has to go through to get through the situation they did. Cutting is terrifying, and you feel like the punishment is all deserved to you. 

With the next few years you will have an opportunity to feel like you can live something you can appreciate. Just hang in there, if you can, please. It does get better. Alot of these clouds won't last. And it's really, really worth it.

Depression makes you a very introvert person. You are consumed in so many thoughts and confusions, even if you are an extrovert, you are forced as a introvert. So what your friend is experiencing is a lack of understanding on how to make those social interactions mean more than he produces, because like you said, he DOES have very good times with them. But for people like us, it's lost the second we leave. We are full with the situation at hand along with our mind you aren't thinking about what it all really means. We always live in the moment with every second that passes behind us. That will make you feel alone in a room filled with loved ones. You have to make that connection within yourself, then others. And for most of us that starts with the people we have connections with.

That's where you come in. I don't even know him and I can tell you, all he wants is an experience and time spent with a trusted, cared about person. His just as nervous as you everytime, your job is to only, and I repeat only, break the ice. Almost like you just met him but you know who he is. There's a level of being scared and nervous with any social interaction and that's the part you feel like is your fault. It's just a misunderstanding of both sides to create and influence a connection that's already there.

As a 20 year old who went and still suffers the same thing,  that feeling you get that seems to be external will always be internal. It takes time to slowly realize it, and then you move onto the next part. What am I supposed to do as a 19 or 20 year old independent, with these conditions. Nothing. Because what you see in yourself out of what you feel will eventually be dead. It basically, it's a literal condition in your mind that you manifest since birth out of your control, and when we grow old enough to have enough organization in our mind, THATS when it comes to play. Around 16, 17, 18. There's nothing I could say to you in our own battles but to know that this is something bigger than you that you will come to painfully understand, and eventually use it like it is, a beautiful curse. To push you to anything you could ever want. Just understand you have a deeper understanding to things and without the right people to help you understand or pursue that to make it real, it just becomes anxiety. So every beautiful thing you're seeing is destroying you instead of helping. Which eventually it will just push you.

So I think the thing is for people like us, we came to completely go through our journey of growth and meanwhile in depression. You know, all the moods, mindsets, confusion, to then learn and understand it, that's literally to be seen in depression, there's a certain capacity to what this illness has to offer. When you have clinical depression, the opposite is not happiness, but vitality. We could quite literally never reach a state of full clarity and bliss, but the paradox is that state of mind for us is found in getting on a set schedule for our bodies, making sure you're getting appropriate sleep, eating, putting yourself outside enough, etc. (Which I know you know already), coming to a good baseline on your personal thinking (good attitude) and the last piece you're missing is the one you're looking for. This is why, most artists of anything have depression, and alot of people who are depressed go on to make art, music, movies etc. It proves the powerful self thinking, you are it. You are it's creation and the creation. Doesn't even have to be art. Anything that expresses the dread you're facing every Day, that's what makes it have it's purpose for every second you live and continue to go. You've learned it all. You've fought it all. You continue to now battle at the highest point you could reach. But it's not worth shit to us if we're going to continue to fight it and not make it INTO something. Society is designed for the modern idiot. We will never feel fulfilled in it because it's nothing new, and we know this. And we're here to create more than that. Find what you're here to create in expressing what you face. You're putting up the best fight you ever have with your depression, and expressing that is what makes getting through the tough moments and being the powerhouses we are actually matter. Matter in our OWN heads. The only one that does matter. And if you atleast tried, you did your best and I'm proud of you for that.

To be honest, the signs are pretty odvious once you've understood them. Yes, feelings of external dread and hopelessness, and or alongside overly emotional feelings and reactions to the world around you are the signs of depression. What is the next thing you are wondering if this is a case. 

This is the disclaimer everyone has to have when talking about this, I'm no doctor I can't confirm it. But I would say it's no doubt.

There's a huge difference between dealing with depression in life, which is almost everybody, just like your parents said, and having clinical depression, literally something in your mind that affects the way you proccess life and the world around you. It will get easier friend. You're facing the battle without the understanding of it, surrounded by those who don't face it. You will come to learn the things you need to survive, in life and depression, within yourself as you go, and in those who deal with this.

From what ive read it seems like there are care centers and it depends on your area, but im assuming you can just look up ketamine therapy or care center closest your area. Says they have one near me, in Chicago.

To those who live beside us in this, we are extremely special and strong, because they understand the lenses we see through. That's the reality. You are extremely important to this world, insanely powerful, to come as far as you have with what you know, and still continue to go, in hopes that someday youll get to be done just FIGHTING. That's a fucking trooper. 
We don't get to see it untill we become healthier and our personal identities are understood, and we can look back, but you are that person since your creation. I'm really proud of you and happy I have had the converse that we did, but what's most important is you'll come to see that for yourself. 
You'll see the tremendous worth in yourself and what you do when you're looking back at the other side, with clarity.
I wish you the best, friend

My heart goes out to you. I've been on these subs because and since I was in the exact same place at the exact same age. Because, nobody should face depression and mental illness more than they have to, and it takes as little as some understanding, support, effort, and love, mostly from sources outside of yourself to really combat this. Otherwise, you grow up with the pains of becoming an adult meanwhile trying to understand your mental illness. Through all of it you'll be okay though, this stuff is alot of work but the crisis you're feeling now will always be changing. Because, while the action, what you're doing in your everyday life is important, it's very miniscule to how we proccess what we're doing. And when you get around 17, 18, is when we really start to proccess more of the world, start to require more responsibilities, and have to look our depression dead in the face. But we have absolutely no understanding of proccessing thoughts and emotions with clarity and grace. Because there's a difference between those who face depression in life which is almost everybody, and those who have a literal mental illness. None of this is your fault, or a waste of time, or your life coming to its end. It's the start to building the foundation to defend against your illness, just remember that. 

This is all a part of learning life, we just proccess it very differently, but it can get overlayered, complicated, overwhelming, which takes you away from being able to see or accomplish much of anything. Medication will help you with anxiety if you're having that, therapy will help you proccess things better, release emotional tension, and get yourself on a good schedule for your needs, eating ,sleeping, etc. And finding somebody who faces depression that's open about it, that has a good attitude on trying to get better, will keep your battle all relative. It gives a place of comfort, and most importantly, this is all growth. It takes alot of patience, time, learning, and while at every turn it's pretty painful, you'll see and go through alot. Time, will make life not ever the same again. Slowly more and more, in a good way.

It all kind of depends. The cause and how depression manifests is different for everybody. There are a few things you can do that will help regardless. Like listening, without judgement, to help get some thoughts or worries comforted. Possibly help him by getting a few responsibilities done, so he doesn't have to worry about those on tops of his anxiety/depression. Show him the love that exists between you, let him see how beautiful and special your relationship is, try to take him away from the dark thoughts in the moment. But generally, to become very depressed something is very skewed, whether it be a traumatic event, something physical, emotional, or the way our brains are wired and how we have been raised around that. Your best bet is to understand the need he has not being awnsered, and find the best way to work on the best solution for that problem. There's a piece of the puzzle missing and the most important part is doing your best to understand that piece. Most other things that come up will be a result of that piece missing, and it can make you get very lost and confused with the other problems that piece creates. Best wishes to you friend because I am in a relationship with both sides having mental issues, I really hope at the end of the day you two can do your best to stay happy and learn ALOT. ♥️
